item.title: Let time accompany you and gradually become rich. Regular investment changes destiny.
item.description:
1 Almost everyone has the qualifications and ability for dollar-cost averaging (DCA).

Highlight(yellow) - Location 135

The DCA strategy includes the following key points: What exactly is the asset? How long is the long-term horizon? How long is the regular interval? What is the minimum amount invested each time?

2 The securities trading market is the ninth great wonder of the world.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 197

People always think that “choosing stocks” is a very difficult thing—actually, it’s not difficult at all! Because the so-called “difficulty” is entirely caused by inertial thinking. In reality, it is merely the result of people being unwilling or afraid to use the simplest, most direct, crude, and effective method. This method is so simple, so unbelievably simple: simply choose the stocks that everyone in the market favors the most.
item.content:encoded:
1 Almost everyone has the qualifications and ability for dollar-cost averaging (DCA).

Highlight(yellow) - Location 135

The DCA strategy includes the following key points: What exactly is the asset? How long is the long-term horizon? How long is the regular interval? What is the minimum amount invested each time?

2 The securities trading market is the ninth great wonder of the world.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 197

People always think that “choosing stocks” is a very difficult thing—actually, it’s not difficult at all! Because the so-called “difficulty” is entirely caused by inertial thinking. In reality, it is merely the result of people being unwilling or afraid to use the simplest, most direct, crude, and effective method. This method is so simple, so unbelievably simple: simply choose the stocks that everyone in the market favors the most.

3 Are there truly investment assets that only rise and never fall?

Highlight(yellow) - Location 260

Therefore, Warren Buffett always recommends that ordinary people buy the S&P 500 index fund—in China, the corresponding asset for the S&P 500 is the CSI 300 index fund. The advantage of index funds is that they are essentially equivalent to “following the market.” You don’t have to bet on the luck of a single company; instead, you bet on the luck of the entire nation, or the luck of the entire world—in any case, in the long run, the scale of the human economy is constantly growing. Look, as long as it is long-term, it suddenly stops being a gamble, because in the long run, risk can actually be diluted to the point of near elimination.

4 The only correct way for ordinary people to invest.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 359

People who “go all in” (put everything on the line) cannot endure pain for too long—in fact, no one can endure pain long-term. This has absolutely nothing to do with so-called “strength.” From another perspective, this isn’t foolishness; it’s merely ignorance. After a month, or two months, or three months of pain, even when looking back, when they feel they are about to get through it, that is, around the sixth month (or slightly before), many people will exit for various reasons—in the trading market, this behavior is called “cutting the meat” (or “cutting losses”). Look, the leeks (investors) cut themselves, and what they cut off is bloody meat.

5 Why few people use the DCA strategy.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 387

6 The profound mechanism behind the magical power of the DCA strategy.

Highlight(yellow) - 6.1. Everyone should cultivate their proactive personality > Location 472

Highlight(yellow) - 6.1. Everyone should cultivate their proactive personality > Location 482

Stay away from those who complain all day—they don’t know what they are doing. They will complain about unfairness with righteous indignation and great spirit, as if Heaven itself is on their side. They never want to know the truth: this world is simply unfair. Using more accurate, unbiased, humble yet confident terms to describe it, this world is full of asymmetry, just as this world is full of uncertainty.

Highlight(yellow) - 6.2. Most proactive people actually don’t know their boundaries > Location 540

As parents themselves, their own future will not improve; their children unconsciously become “people who have always been passive toward themselves.” The correct choice should originally be: parents should proactively make themselves better and better; causing the children to desire improvement out of envy, and thus the children will take the initiative, even if it is merely superficial imitation, which is a good start.

Highlight(yellow) - 6.4. The optimal strategy for riding the trend must be proactive passivity > Location 636

Whether a decision is significant or meaningful, just look at one metric: Is it a choice aligned with the trend?

Highlight(yellow) - 6.4. The optimal strategy for riding the trend must be proactive passivity > Location 665

Highlight(yellow) - 6.5. DCA is the best practice strategy for “proactive passivity” > Location 680

Highlight(yellow) - 6.6. How powerful is the passive force of following the trend? > Location 772

The longer the investment cycle, the greater the advantage of passivity; the larger the investment amount, the greater the advantage of passivity.

Highlight(yellow) - 6.7. How much space do you still have within the proactive boundary? > Location 818

The truth has no obligation to cater to your emotions.

Highlight(yellow) - 6.8. The long-term perspective determines your result > Location 868

If you feel desperate, it is merely because you are currently poor. If your feeling is very desperate, it is merely because you are truly poor.

Highlight(yellow) - 6.8. The long-term perspective determines your result > Location 872

The poorer you are, the more patience you need. What is courage? Courage is the only virtue that cannot be faked.

Highlight(yellow) - 6.8. The long-term perspective determines your result > Location 903

One rise is not a trend, and one fall is not a trend; one rise plus one fall constitutes a cycle; judging the trend requires at least two cycles. After two cycles, the two fluctuations formed can only be one of three trends: rising, horizontal, or falling.

Highlight(yellow) - 6.9. What extreme advantage do ordinary people possess? > Location 992

More than ten years ago, I occasionally heard two middle managers from a large company discussing how to make their subordinates obedient: “Alas, how did you manage to make them obedient? I’m really worried!"—Isn’t it simple? Organize a group of wives to go look at houses together! Let me tell you, don’t look down on them now that they are acting so powerful in front of you; as long as they buy a house, paying the down payment today, tomorrow they are mine! No doubt about it!

7 The difference between foolishness and ignorance, and passive intelligence.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1068

8 Some people are always on the correct side.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1147

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1178

For all ordinary people, the DCA strategy is absolutely feasible, completely genuine, and relies entirely on yourself. The “ordinary people” referred to here are not distinguished by race, nationality, region, gender, age, height, weight, beauty, or ugliness, nor by sexual orientation… The key is that they are not even distinguished by IQ and education level!

9 The common appearance on the other side of the mirror world.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1202

Their explanations are always astonishingly consistent: “Alas, I am just too greedy!”

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1210

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1226

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1249

10 DCA is the essential choice for ordinary people.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1296

There are three conditions that determine a person’s wealth: background, luck, and effort; and among these three, effort is the most insignificant.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1337

Conclusion

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1405

Within your proactive boundary, continuously strengthen your psychological construction and desperately find ways to make money outside the market; at the same time, outside the proactive boundary, proactively choose an asset absolutely worth holding long-term, and use the money you earned outside the market to invest regularly… Over time, you can harness the magical passive power generated by the trend, not only potentially break free from the shackles of class solidification, but even change your destiny—ultimately, gain freedom.

Note - Location 1408

National destiny seems to be a ultimate asset, I should DCA into the S&P 500.

item.title: The Path to Financial Freedom_Li Xiaolai
item.description:
00.20160729 Three Iron Laws of Selling Time ★

Highlight(blue) - Location 163

The three iron laws of selling time: Growth is the fundamental key, prioritize value over valuation, and patience is more important than anything else.

Highlight(blue) - Location 167

The so-called personal financial freedom means that a person no longer has to sell their time just to meet basic living necessities.

Highlight(orange) - Location 203

There is only one standard for selection: Can what I choose help me accumulate more ability?
item.content:encoded:
00.20160729 Three Iron Laws of Selling Time ★

Highlight(blue) - Location 163

The three iron laws of selling time: Growth is the fundamental key, prioritize value over valuation, and patience is more important than anything else.

Highlight(blue) - Location 167

The so-called personal financial freedom means that a person no longer has to sell their time just to meet basic living necessities.

Highlight(orange) - Location 203

There is only one standard for selection: Can what I choose help me accumulate more ability?

Highlight(blue) - Location 204

Now that food delivery is so developed, when I go to pick up takeout, I often think: so many people are selling their time at such cheap prices, and what they are doing is something that has absolutely no accumulation effect. What will they do in the future?

Highlight(blue) - Location 207

If you don’t need to break through, then you don’t need to grow, and you don’t need to learn further. Doing such a job might give you some self-satisfaction (mostly from stability), but because there is no growth, you can never cross a milestone in your lifetime.

Highlight(pink) - Location 245

It is a habit, because the short-term gains from deception are always very high. In the long run, this habit is almost impossible to eradicate. You see, the reason it is hard to adhere to the iron laws is because the temptation to violate them is too great. But looking at it the other way, all deceptions are not permanent; there will always be a day when the truth comes out. From this perspective, the advice given by Dario of Bridgewater is truly wise.

Highlight(pink) - Location 253

People who lack patience are more likely to choose “end-point thinking.” They hope to finish quickly, see results quickly, and then they can enter the world they have imagined. Lack of patience…

01.20160801 Three Major Pitfalls Hindering Financial Freedom ★

Highlight(yellow) - Location 278

  1. You must focus all your most precious attention on your own “growth.” 2. Entrepreneurship is growth. Without growth, it is not entrepreneurship. 3. People who don’t cherish their attention are destined to be poor in the end, because they will be harvested their entire lives, and they will never have truly valuable output. How can they eventually become wealthy?

Highlight(yellow) - Location 291

The first major pitfall is called “randomly joining the fun.”

Highlight(yellow) - Location 298

The online world has even more fun; you can even brew yourself a cup of tea, strike a pose, and watch. Oh! Vanke had an incident! Oh! Wu Yifan had an incident! Oh! Zhao Wei had an incident! Oh… These people are now called “melon-eaters” (spectators) online. Compared to those watching on the roadside, online spectators turn joining the fun into a farce—a group of people are inexplicably watching, and as they watch, the spectators start arguing with each other, attracting even more people… It is said that curiosity is the source of creativity. Look, in fact, everyone has abundant curiosity. Unfortunately, it is wasted on watching inexplicable fun. However, this is also right…

Highlight(yellow) - Location 305

The second major pitfall is called “rushing to follow the trend.” Suddenly, a certain “trend” appears. For example, the recent “content entrepreneurship,” or last year’s “O2O”… Something is hot! Instantly, a large group of people (in fact, always the vast majority) rush to follow the trend… But they forget that whenever a major trend appears, there is always another group of people who were already prepared—even if they weren’t intentionally prepared. If content entrepreneurship is truly a trend, a major tide, then the group of people who have been writing for ten years before this are clearly “unintentionally but inevitably the most prepared.” The people who just started rushing, how can they compete with the other group?

Highlight(yellow) - Location 318

The third major pitfall is called “worrying about others’ hearts.”

Highlight(yellow) - Location 330

—A saying: You are a mud Bodhisattva, unable to cross even a small river, yet you worry about others’ hearts. Truly, what are you aiming for? If someone fails in their business, you won’t suffer a loss, but if someone succeeds, you are afraid, aren’t you?

Highlight(yellow) - Location 345

Money is not the most important thing because it can regenerate; time is also not the most important thing because it essentially doesn’t belong to you. You can only try to be friends with it and make it work for you. Your attention is the most important and precious resource you possess—viewed from this angle, life is actually fair, because your attention is something you can control yourself, unless you give it up. So, whether the outcome is good or bad, it is truly up to you.

Note - Location 348

Attention

Highlight(blue) - Location 351

This might be the most valuable advice in life—because, ultimately, all your value is the output of your attention. Moreover, more critically, a person’s attention is likely the only resource that can be called “innate” and productive. Think about it, what else is like this?… Where should it be placed? The answer is clear and unique: placed on “growth.” There is a Silicon Valley “cliché” that is actually very meaningful: “Entrepreneurship is growth. Without growth, it is not entrepreneurship.”

Highlight(blue) - Location 359

If you want to go one step further, you can try listing the following (this is not homework): 1. Review what you have been paying attention to? List them, and judge whether those things are related to you? Are they related to your growth? 2. Review what you have been paying attention to last week? List them? Judge whether those things are related to you? Are they related to your growth? 3. Review what you have been paying attention to last month… I know you probably can’t remember it?

Highlight(blue) - Location 365

In a sense, advertising is actually this kind of business model, isn’t it? You can study the major marketing accounts on Weibo; they are best at “attracting attention”—another way of saying “harvesting cheap or free attention.” Then look at how many people are even “voluntarily contributing their attention,” and then you can understand why this business model can ultimately achieve “long-lasting prosperity.”

Highlight(pink) - Location 370

If you dare to ignore your attention, your attention (in fact, your attention is the truly valuable you) will be ruthlessly harvested and sold.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 373

People who don’t cherish their attention are destined to be poor in the end, because they will be harvested their entire lives, and they will never have truly valuable output. How can they eventually become wealthy?

01.20160805 Our Most Important Wealth is “Attention” ★

Highlight(blue) - Location 385

Keywords: Accumulation Effect, Key to Happiness, Individual Value 1. When some people ask why their schedule is packed yet they still feel they have no gain, I remind them: the packed thing is your time; the idle thing is your attention; the wasted thing is your growth. 2. Put your attention on your own growth. Put it on skills that can have an accumulation effect, and then give them sufficient learning, thinking, and refinement. 3. Put your attention on true love without expecting return; this is the key to true happiness. 4. Put your attention on things that truly contribute to society. Individual value equals one’s social contribution rate.

Highlight(blue) - Location 425

The wasted thing is your growth.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 455

Reasons for falling into the three major attention pitfalls: For most people, short-term pleasure is more useful than long-term gain. It satisfies personal so-called security, belonging, and achievement.

02.20160812 Paying is Picking Up Bargains ★

Highlight(blue) - Location 463

  1. What bargains have you picked up by paying in the past period? Not just this channel—this channel is super valuable, without a doubt. 2. In the past period, where have you wasted time and attention in places where you could have picked up bargains? 3. In the past period, how many times have you been in a bad mood all day because of an argument with family? 4. If you need continuous attention but are repeatedly disturbed, have you thought of any effective countermeasures? 5. Where have you ignored the value order of assets, to the point where you suffered a big loss?

Highlight(yellow) - Location 471

What resource is most important? (Attention) What resource is more important? (Attention > Time > Money)

Highlight(yellow) - Location 479

Many people comment, saying they don’t know what to do with their attention. O Accumulate knowledge O Refine skills O Observe life O Think about the future O Create value O Manage relationships

Highlight(yellow) - Location 512

Things to guard against.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 513

So, I have long invented my own method: always set the phone to silent, and turn off all push notifications. When I am focused on working, I should not accept any disturbance. When I stop and rest, I can handle the unread messages and missed calls.

Highlight(pink) - Location 527

Because overall, paying money to buy time is more worthwhile!

Highlight(pink) - Location 557

The best way to make others approach you is to occasionally do something admirable.

03.20160819 The Heaviest Shackle of Life is “Security” ★

Highlight(blue) - Location 561

  1. Almost all progress is achieved by giving up some security. 2. Pursuing 100% security will definitely trap you in the eternal present. 3. We must give up some security to deeply observe and think long-term. 4. Don’t cooperate with people who lack security—because in their world, a true cooperative relationship is actually impossible. 5. Regarding reading, put your attention on how to apply the knowledge gained to improve your life.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 573

Most people are like this: constantly paying attention to everything around them that can be paid attention to, and they are very afraid that they might miss something. They cannot concentrate long-term, nor can they think deeply long-term; their attention is always focused on every event happening around them. Such people have no past, and no future; they don’t even know that they could have a past and a future. For them, there is only the present without comparison.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 580

Ultimately, this may lead to being trapped in the eternal present.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 583

In a sense: almost all progress is achieved by giving up some security.

Highlight(orange) - Location 588

…rather, it is to pursue the security of “not being left behind by the times.” Believe it or not, look around you at how many people are pursuing 100% security. They are constantly attracted by everything happening around them; they cannot deeply observe or deeply think about anything—this might not be their nature, but it is simply that they themselves haven’t realized the limitations of this survival mode—they are like those animals, trapped in the eternal present.

Highlight(orange) - Location 604

One of them is not taking risks.

Highlight(orange) - Location 616

What is cooperation? The essence of cooperation is that everyone gives up a small part of their security and entrusts that part of security to the partner. What is trust? Trust is believing that the other party will not exploit the part of security you voluntarily give up.

Highlight(orange) - Location 623

The so-called lack of security is actually not believing that others can refrain from exploiting the part of security you give up, so they must secure 100% themselves—this is truly an exhausting state, isn’t it? If you know what the root of people’s lack of security is, you will understand why this advice is correct: don’t cooperate with people who lack security—because in their world, a true cooperative relationship is actually impossible.

Highlight(orange) - Location 646

100% security brings 100% constraint.

Highlight(orange) - Location 647

Your time and attention are fleeting; try not to waste them on rapidly depreciating information.

04.20160826 The Foundation of Life: “Having a Future” ★

Highlight(blue) - Location 691

• In the long run, the output rate of brain power will definitely be higher than the output rate of physical strength, and by many orders of magnitude… • The glass ceiling for physical strength is obvious, but the glass ceiling for brain power is unknown… • The time for physical strength decline comes very early, but the time for brain power decline comes much later… • The huge profits gained through brute force are decreasing, because in the major trend, knowledge is more likely to generate greater huge profits…

Highlight(blue) - Location 753

Don’t expect to be correct in one go.

Highlight(blue) - Location 760

So-called investment is nothing more than exchanging current resources for future resources.

05.20160902 How to Meet a Benefactor ★

Highlight(blue) - Location 774

Belief combined with patience is what can help you endure accidental setbacks and wait for inevitable good fortune. Often, what hinders our action is not our own ability, but the wrong concepts in our minds.

Highlight(blue) - Location 878

  1. Optimistic people are more likely to become benefactors to others; 2. Benefactors are more likely to meet benefactors; 3. Those who can help others progress are true benefactors; 4. Excellent people, respected people are more likely to receive help; 5. People who are willing to share are more likely to receive help; 6. People who don’t burden others are more likely to receive help; 7. People who are not ashamed to ask for help are more likely to receive help; 8. When asking for help, it is not appropriate to rely only on money as a return; when helping others, it is not appropriate to charge money in return; 9. A benefactor is not necessarily a genius; a genius is often just busy with themselves, but a benefactor is different; they often “value harmony over genius,” and better understand “the collective is more valuable than the individual.”

Highlight(blue) - Location 882

…the collective is more valuable than the individual. 10. Often, people’s success comes from a large number of people hoping to see them succeed. Conversely, if a large number of people are unwilling to see someone succeed, then this person will find it difficult to receive so-called “benefactor assistance”; 11. People who are doing the right thing are more likely to receive benefactor assistance; this is what “many helping the virtuous” means; 12. People who live in the future are more likely to meet benefactors, because others can see the future in them.

Highlight(orange) - Location 899

Not “asking for help.”

06.20160909 Regarding “Capital” ★

Highlight(orange) - Location 958

Capital is indeed mainly composed of money, but just a pile of money placed there is certainly not capital.

Highlight(orange) - Location 1001

In the investment environment, earning 50% profit with 10,000 RMB as capital, compared to earning 15% profit with 100,000 RMB as capital, the former performs better, or to be slightly more professional, the former has a higher capital efficiency than the latter.

Highlight(blue) - Location 1006

The fundamental reason they buy junk stocks is because “that thing is cheap.” They focus on absolute value, so even if a stock has high profit potential, as soon as they look at the price and “feel it’s too expensive,” they turn and leave.

Highlight(blue) - Location 1022

In other words, a person with an annual income of 60,000 RMB, taking out 5,000 RMB as investment capital and “sentencing” this capital to a life sentence, will actually, in a high probability, not affect their quality of life.

Highlight(blue) - Location 1024

One of the secrets to acquiring wealth is not taking risks. Giving up security allows you to have more energy to focus on specific fields, observe long-term, and think deeply, rather than encouraging everyone to take risks.

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1052

Becoming an outstanding investor is only a matter of time, first because they have started; and it is equivalent to already “winning at the starting line,” because the initial act of “sentencing their own capital to a life sentence” has laid the most solid foundation for them to develop the ability to “think deeply about the future” later. With this foundation, many skills are unnecessary, many traps automatically disappear, and many helpless anxieties instantly vanish… I know you might feel that “life sentence” is both cruel and unnecessary—but this is the wisdom you must acquire: struggling to learn how to distinguish between…

07.20160916 Regarding “Falling Behind” ★

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1220

  1. Sooner or later, you will achieve the state of not selling your time just for a living. 2. Sooner or later, you will achieve the state of not falling behind, becoming in the top 20%, or even the top 1%.

08.20160923 The Best Strategy to Move from Mediocrity to Excellence: “Multi-dimensional Competition” ★

Highlight(yellow) - Location 1252

Highlight(yellow) - Location 5941

The key is: before starting, you conduct in-depth research and reach a fairly certain conclusion: this is a company with extremely strong growth potential… Because, your return = company growth potential x fixed investment strategy utility. If the company’s growth potential is zero, then the utility of the fixed investment strategy is equivalent to zero; if it is ultimately proven that the company not only hasn’t grown, but has even declined, then the utility of the fixed investment strategy is effectively equivalent to magnifying the loss.

item.title: 10 Principles of Economics
item.description:
1. People face trade-offs.
  2. The cost of some things is what you give up to get them.
  3. Rational people consider marginal quantities.
  4. People react to incentives when they trade with each other.
  5. Trade can make everyone better off.
  6. The market is usually a good way to organize economic activity.
  7. Government sometimes can improve market outcomes and how the entire economy runs.
  8. A country’s standard of living depends on its ability to produce goods and services.
  9. When the government issues too much currency, prices rise.
  10. Society faces the short-run trade-off between inflation and unemployment.

item.title: Get Paid for Your Judgment

item.title: Don’t play zero-sum games
item.description: The article explores the dynamics between wealth creation as a positive-sum game and status as a zero-sum game, highlighting how some people attack wealth creation in pursuit of status.
item.content:encoded:
The business world has many people playing zero sum games and a few playing positive sum games searching for each other in the crowd.

Wealth creation is an evolutionarily recent positive-sum game. Status is an old zero-sum game. Those attacking wealth creation are often just seeking status.

item.title: Little Dog Money Summary
item.description: Some people who read this book cannot take in what you say, so there is no change. Others, after reading it, begin to be smart about geography and finance, and they will have a happier and richer life.
item.content:encoded:
The Foundation of Wealth Building

Financial freedom is a goal that anyone today can achieve, of course, this requires us to have the courage to pursue the life we truly desire. As a famous saying goes: “It is not the difficulty that makes us give up, but rather that we give up, which makes it seem so difficult.”

If we keep the laws of money in mind, we will find that our financial situation is steadily improving. Nothing can stop a mindset that aligns with the times. This also applies to everyone’s life. Nothing can stop us from enjoying the right we are born with—wealth. A life of dignity and financial comfort aligns with our natural laws. As long as we don’t give up, nothing can prevent us from reaching this goal.

Making a Dream Album

To achieve financial freedom, we must have motivation. Therefore, the first thing we must do is think up 10 reasons (wishes) why we want to become wealthy, and write them down. This will be the driving force for our actions.

Next, from these 10 reasons for wanting to become wealthy, select the top 3 most important ones. Don’t set yourself too many goals, as that might be unrealistic. Human desires are endless, and we need to distinguish between primary and secondary, determining which are the most important goals. After setting the goals, we must find ways to achieve them.

One method taught by Qianqian to Jia is to use a Dream Album and a Dream Piggy Bank: the Dream Album is used to collect photos related to your wishes, and you paste them into the album.

Looking at the Album Daily

The act of thinking through pictures and imagining the scenarios where you achieve your wishes is called “visualization.”

Preparing a Dream Piggy Bank

Prepare a piggy bank for each dream, and write your dream on it. Once the piggy bank is ready, save every penny you save into it.

When Jia doubted whether the Dream Album would be effective, Qianqian said: “Curiosity is good, but it must never hinder your actions. Too many people hesitate in their actions simply because they feel they haven’t fully understood the matter. Putting it into practice is much more useful than pure thinking.”

When we question whether this fantasy is a “pipe dream,” we need to know that “successful people are successful because they always dream of the day they succeed, constantly imagining the situation when they have achieved their dreams. Of course, people cannot remain stuck in dreams.”

“Learning is the process of recognizing new concepts and new ideas. If people always consider problems using the same way of thinking, they will always get the same results. Don’t jump to conclusions before you have done it.”

People without imagination find it difficult to achieve great things. The more effort we put into something, the greater the possibility of success. But most people put their energy into things they don’t like, instead of imagining what they hope to gain.

Don’t approach it with a “let’s try” mindset; take concrete action! If you only approach it with a “let’s try” mindset, it will only end in failure, and we will achieve nothing. ‘Trying’ is merely an excuse; before we even try, we have already prepared an escape route for ourselves. There is no option to ’try’; there are only two choices—to do it or not to do it."

Success Journal

When we do something, we need sufficient self-confidence. Our level of confidence determines whether we believe in our ability and whether we believe in ourselves. If we fundamentally don’t believe we can do it, we won’t even start, and if we don’t start, we will gain nothing."

Therefore, we need to keep a “Success Journal.” The “Success Journal” is similar to a diary; record all the things you have successfully done in it, writing down at least 5 personal achievements every day, no matter how small. The main purpose of doing this is to help us boost our self-confidence.

At the beginning, we might feel it’s difficult, and we might ask ourselves, “Can this or that thing really be counted as an achievement?” In this case, our answer should be affirmative. Being overly confident is much better than being insufficiently confident."

When we encounter problems:

a. Still stick to your idea Everyone can do this when things are normal. It is only when true difficulties arise that the difference becomes clear. Only a few people can firmly implement their plans. Very successful people even have the ability to perform exceptionally when things are at their most difficult.

b. When progress is smooth Even when everything is progressing very smoothly, you must firmly stick to your plan.

c. The 72-Hour Rule When we decide to do something, we must complete it within 72 hours, otherwise, we are likely to never do it again."

“How much money a person earns is linked to their self-confidence. Furthermore, whether their experiences are focused within their scope of ability or placed outside of what they can achieve is also very important. Without a Success Journal, we won’t think about in which areas we are suited to earn money.”

Often, our inability to act stems from the psychology of fear. Fear always appears when we imagine how things might go wrong. The more we think about the possibility of failure, the more afraid we become. But when we look at our Success Journal, we notice the successful things, and naturally, we think about how to do them."

Earning and Saving Money

When Qianqian encouraged Jia to bravely earn money, she told the story of a young boy named Darryl. Darryl became a millionaire at the age of 17 through personal effort, making him a role model for Jia.

In Darryl’s story, a businessman gave Darryl (Jia’s role model) advice on earning money:

  1. Figure out what you like, and then figure out how to earn money from it.
  2. Solve a problem for others, and you will earn a lot of money;
  3. Focus your energy on what you know, what you can do, and what you possess.
  4. Before buying something, ask yourself, “Is this really necessary?”

Mr. Jin, when guiding Jia not to spend all the money she had immediately, told the story of a goose that lays golden eggs:

A goose raised by a farmer lays a golden egg every day. The farmer was very greedy and hoped the goose would lay at least two golden eggs every day. In a fit of pique, he killed the goose, and from then on, he never received another golden egg. The goose is the principal, and the golden egg is the interest. The farmer’s biggest mistake was not “killing” his “goose.”

Expenditure and income are directly proportional; the higher the income, the higher the expenditure, unless you learn to allocate your assets reasonably and learn to spend within your means.

Advice for Those in Debt:

a. Destroy all credit cards Spending with a credit card costs more than spending with cash.

b. Pay the minimum installment amount within the allowed limit The higher the installment amount, the less living money you have left each month. Often, people underestimate how high their living expenses are, and they might take out new loans to pay off old ones when a large expense occurs.

c. For consumer loans For loans for goods in daily life, such as a TV loan, it is best not to apply for it first. If you do apply, save half of the money remaining after deducting living expenses, and use the other half to pay the consumer loan.

Fund Allocation

The author suggests that we can divide our income into Daily Expenses (10%) + Dream Goals (40%) + Golden Goose Account (50%). This means we can save 50% of our income, and this money should not be easily touched; it is like the goose mentioned earlier that lays golden eggs, allowing money to generate more money.

Of the remaining 50%, besides the 10% needed for daily life, the remaining 40% is saved to achieve the dreams we want, such as buying a phone as a reward for yourself, or going on a trip, etc. This amount is up to you to manage and plan; remember to allocate it reasonably.

Golden Goose: From the story of laying golden eggs, the “goose” refers to the money (savings value), and the “golden egg” refers to the interest.

Never kill your goose, and don’t use all your money to pay off loans, leaving yourself with nothing. Having nothing is not our goal; our goal is to achieve the initial 3 wishes or accumulate the savings.

Passive Income

Investment Tips:

  1. Invest money in a safe place.
  2. Money should lay many “golden eggs” (choose high interest, with the highest dividends coming from stocks).
  3. Investment should be simple and clear, easy to operate.

The 72 Rule:

Divide 72 by the annual profit percentage of the investment, and the resulting number is the number of years required for that money to double.

Divide 72 by a certain inflation rate, and you can find out how many years it will take for the money to lose half its value.

When the market declines, losses only occur when you actually sell the fund.

A fund has an indicator—the Fluctuation Rate (Volatility): a lower fluctuation rate means higher safety and more stable profit growth. Funds generally last 5 to 10 years; the market always has ups and downs, but the overall trend is upward, so you can check the market after 5 or 10 years.

72 / Return Rate = Time to Double 72 / Inflation Rate = Time to Half Value 115 Rule: 115 / Return Rate = Time to Double

Controlling Risk

Cash Reserves are Necessary

You cannot put all your money into stocks or funds; you must reserve some cash to have liquid funds, so that when the stock market declines, you can buy appropriately at the right time. The remaining reserve cash can be invested in short-term income projects, such as daily deposits. Bank passbooks are merely money-swallowing machines; their returns are often less than the losses caused by inflation. Some savings accounts have high interest rates, but they require keeping the cash in the bank for a relatively long time, so the author does not recommend relying solely on bank passbooks.

Qianqian’s Words

Some people who read this book do not absorb what you say, and thus make no changes. Others, after reading it, begin to manage their finances wisely, and they will lead happier and wealthier lives.

item.title: Why risk keeping so much money and gold at home?
item.description: “There are many reasons,” the old lady explained to me, “First, because sometimes I just like holding these things to admire them. I really like gold and banknotes.” I looked at her with slight disagreement, thinking to myself that liking money in this way—I wonder if it’s normal—and she admits it so frankly… But then I recalled that day, when Marcel and I were looking at the things in the box and counting them one by one. How delightful it was when we touched each gold bar! Shouldn’t an old lady enjoy the same sense of happiness when opening a box? Besides, these things belong to her. Mrs. Tao Mu continued, “Second, this money is kept for emergencies. No matter what happens, the things in the box will be enough for me to live on for several years.” “That’s a bit too much, isn’t it!” I said with a laugh. “That depends on how much money you have in total,” Mrs. Tao Mu explained. “If you keep cash at home that is more than 10% of your total assets, then it’s meaningless.” I whistled softly. This old lady must be very wealthy. “Third, I have invested a large portion of the money in stocks, which involves a certain risk. So, it is wise to keep a portion of the money readily available. I can explain this to you in more detail another time.”

item.title: If they didn't have to worry about money, they could live very well.
item.description: To live a happier and more satisfying life, one must change oneself. This has nothing to do with money; money itself neither makes people happy nor brings misfortune. Money is neutral; it is neither good nor bad. Only when money belongs to a specific person will it exert a positive or negative influence on that person. Money can be used for good purposes, or it can be used for bad ones. A happy person will be happier when they have money; conversely, a pessimistic or anxious person will have more worries the more money they possess.

item.title: But Monica's parents' financial situation is getting better, isn't it?
item.description: Soon, I turned 12. Everything was still the same; we still didn’t go on vacation by the sea. Mom and Dad kept saying that business was affected by the “economic recession.” What they meant was that the domestic economic situation was the root cause of their financial problems. But I had a question: why was my friend Monica’s parents’ financial situation getting better and better, even with the same economic situation?

item.title: It's not trying, but taking action!
item.description: If you only approach things with a “try-it-out” mindset, then you will ultimately end in failure, and you will achieve nothing. Trying is purely an excuse; before you even do it, you have already prepared an escape route for yourself. If you can’t test, you only have two choices—do it or don’t do it. Too many people hesitate when doing things simply because they feel they haven’t fully grasped something. And actually putting it into practice is much smarter than pure thinking.

item.title: Most people don't know what they truly want, they only know that they want more.
item.description: You can imagine your life as a very large mail-order company. If you write to a mail-order company saying, “Please send me some good things,” you certainly won’t receive anything. The same goes for our wishes. We must know exactly what we truly desire in our hearts.

item.title: The desire to compensate for losses was so intense that one forgot the risks being undertaken.
item.description: The more significant a potential loss, the stronger our aversion to loss. In other words, the more dangerous the situation, the more likely we are to quickly make irrational decisions.

item.title: Holy Book *Naval Compendium: Guide to Wealth and Happiness*
item.description: Naval Ravikant's profound insights on wealth, knowledge, decision-making, and happiness, helping you build a more successful and fulfilling life.
item.content:encoded:
1. People Should Seek Wealth, Not Money or Status

People should not earn wealth through arduous work. Working 80 hours a week in a restaurant will not make you richer. Hard work is unavoidable, but it should be done in the right way. People should seek wealth, not money or status. If you believe wealth is unimportant, wealth will move away from you. Wealth is assets that continue to make money while you sleep. Without wealth-generating assets, when you sleep, you have no income; when you retire, you cannot keep earning money. In short, without wealth, you cannot achieve non-linear earning. Generally, wealth is created by starting your own company or by investing. Neither of these is achieved by putting in a massive amount of time; the ultra-rich, just like you, only have 24 hours every day.

2. The Key to Acquiring Wealth

To acquire wealth, you can provide something valuable to the masses—especially something they don’t know how to obtain. And you must supply it on a large scale. The internet has greatly expanded career possibilities, and most people still lack a clear understanding of this. Learn marketing, learn creation. If you master these two things, nothing can stop you from succeeding.

3. Arm Yourself with Special Knowledge

Special knowledge is knowledge that cannot be acquired through training. If it can be acquired through training, others can also acquire it, and they can replace you. Special knowledge is usually high in technical sophistication and creative. It cannot be outsourced or automated. (For example, insight) It can be discovered when driven by genuine curiosity and passion. The process of creating special knowledge feels like playing to you, but like working to others. Usually, special knowledge lies at the boundaries of knowledge—things that are either newly understood or genuinely difficult to understand. If you do not commit 100%, someone who commits 100% will surpass you. And they won’t just be slightly better; they will be much better, because in the realm of ideas, compound interest will work, and leverage will work. Special knowledge might be things like: Sales skills. Having musical talent. Persistence: This means you can research things with dedication. Loving science fiction: This means you can quickly absorb a lot of knowledge. Playing many games: This means you have a good understanding of game theory. Gossip: This might help you become a very interesting journalist. Special knowledge is a strange combination, coming from your DNA, your unique environment of growth, and your response to that knowledge. These are almost integrated into your personality and identity, and then you can continuously refine them. Study microeconomics, game theory, psychology, brainwashing techniques, ethics, mathematics, and computer science.

4. Arm Yourself with Leverage

Business leverage mainly consists of capital, labor, and products with extremely low replication costs (code and media). Capital refers to money. To raise funds, you need to use your special knowledge, combined with your sense of responsibility, to demonstrate your good judgment. Labor refers to the people who work for you. It is the oldest and most fiercely contested form of leverage. Labor leverage will make your parents feel proud, but don’t waste your life pursuing this alone. Capital and labor are forms of leverage that require permission to use. Everyone chases capital, but there must always be someone to pay for it. Everyone wants to lead others, but there must always be subordinates. Code and media are forms of leverage that require no permission; they are the leverage behind the new rich. You can create software and media that work for you even while you sleep. A large group of robots is available for free use—to save space and energy efficiency, they are packaged into data centers; use them! By applying special knowledge combined with leverage, you will ultimately get what you deserve.

5. In One Sentence: Productize Yourself

What does this mean? “Productize” and “yourself.” “Yourself” has uniqueness; “productize” has leverage. “Am I productizing it? Can I scale it? Can I amplify it through labor, capital, code, or media?” So, this phrase is very easy to remember. If you want to be richer, you must figure out what you can provide to society that society doesn’t know how to obtain, but that society wants, and providing it to you is natural and within your skill set and capability. Next, you must find a way to scale it, because producing only one is far from enough. You might need to produce thousands, or tens of thousands, or millions, or even billions, so that everyone can have one. Steve Jobs (and his team, of course) figured out that society needed a smartphone. This smartphone had all the functions of phones at the time, but also many other new functions, and it was easier to use. Therefore, they figured out how to manufacture the smartphone, and then they figured out how to mass-produce the smartphone. You must become the person who can scale the provision of these products or services. This is the real challenge of how to make money.

6. Pay Attention to Your Character

In my life, I have known some extremely successful, very popular, and very smart people. However, I have seen them do one or two things that were not very good for others. I would say, “Hey, I think you shouldn’t do this to others. Because it will ultimately hurt yourself.” Deep down, we all know who we are. You cannot hide anything from yourself. You are very clear whether what you do is right or wrong; if you have too many moral flaws, you will not respect yourself. The worst outcome in this world is a lack of self-respect. If you don’t love yourself, who will love you? If I see someone doing this, the first time I will remind them, but usually they won’t change, and then I will keep my distance from them. I cut them out of my life. If someone constantly claims to be honest, they are likely dishonest. These are just some effective indicators that I have learned. When someone spends a lot of time talking about their values or talking about themselves, it means they are hiding something. I think to myself: “If you want to get close to me, your values must be better than mine.”

7. Smart People Truly Understand One Thing

If someone uses many complex words and many grand concepts, they are likely unaware of what they are actually talking about. I believe the smartest people can explain things to a child. If you cannot explain it to a child, then you don’t truly know it. Truly smart thinkers are clear-thinking thinkers; they understand very, very basic foundational knowledge.

8. Step Outside Yourself to See the Truth

Imagine one of my friends is going through some difficulties, such as a breakup, career issues, business failure, or health problems. When he needs my advice, it often takes me only a few minutes to accurately tell him, “Oh, that girl, forget her. Anyway, she’s not good for you. You will be happier. Believe me. You will find someone more suitable in the future.” But he himself finds it difficult to see this. Because he is in pain and torment, his desires conflict with reality, which prevents him from seeing the truth clearly. The same thing happens when we make decisions. To see the truth clearly, you must set aside the self, because the self does not want to face the truth.

9. What is Truly Important is Leisure Time

Great ideas only come after you feel bored. Good ideas never appear when you are under pressure, busy, rushing around, or in a hurry. If your schedule doesn’t have one or two days a week where you aren’t constantly in meetings or constantly busy, you cannot think. You won’t have good ideas related to your business. You also cannot make good judgments. I encourage you to set aside at least one day a week (better yet, two days, because if you prepare two days, you will definitely find one) so that you have time to think. Cherish your time; it is everything. It is more important than your money. It is more important than your friends. It is more important than anything. Your time is everything. Don’t waste your time.

10. Reading Can Make You Successful

Spending one hour a day reading science, mathematics, and philosophy can likely put you on the high ladder of human success within seven years. I have spent a lot of time reading. My only true friend is books. Books are great friends because they tell you the wisdom of the best thinkers over the past thousands of years. Any book that has survived for two thousand years has been screened by many people, and it is more likely to be correct; I want to reread these books. The fact is, I read not for self-improvement. I read out of curiosity and interest. The best book is the one that captivates you.

11. Do Things for Your Own Goals

I truly want to do things for my own goals. Whether it is business, fitness, romance, friendship, or anything else, I believe the meaning of life is to do things for your own goals. When you do things for yourself, you can create your best work. Even if you do these things to make money, you will actually be the most successful. Follow your true curiosity, not the current hot topics. If your curiosity leads you to where society will eventually go, you will receive rich rewards. When you are dating, there is a moment you realize that the relationship will not lead to marriage, you might be better off moving on. When you are learning something, such as geography or history, and you realize you will never use this information, drop that course. That is wasting time. That is wasting mental energy.

12. Become a Better Decision-Maker Overall

Become a better decision-maker overall. Decision-making is everything. Yes. Decision-making is everything. In fact, someone who makes correct decisions 80% of the time instead of 70% of the time will have value and compensation in the market hundreds of times higher. I believe people find it difficult to understand a basic fact of leverage. If I manage $1 billion, and I am often 10% more correct than others, my decisions can bring $100 million in value in a single judgment. With modern technology, massive labor, and capital, the multiplier of our decisions can be leveraged to increasingly higher levels. If I face a difficult choice, such as these questions: Should I marry this person? Should I take this job? Should I buy this house? Should I move to this city? Should I partner with this person in business? If you cannot decide, answer no. The reason is that modern society is full of choices. There are so many choices. We live on a planet with 7 billion people, and we can connect with everyone through the internet. There are hundreds of thousands of professions for you to choose from. There are so many choices. When you choose certain things, you are locked in for a very long time. Starting a business might take 10 years. Starting a relationship might take 5 years or more. Moving to a city might take 10 to 20 years. These are all decisions with very, very long-term impact. We only say “yes” when we are very certain. You can never be absolutely certain, but you must be very confident. If you have two choices, and they are relatively equal, then choose the path that is more difficult and more painful in the short term. The reality is that one path will endure short-term pain. The other path will feel pain further down the line in the future. However, your brain tries to avoid conflict and tries to avoid short-term pain. By definition, if two choices are similar, and one has short-term pain, then this choice is related to long-term gain. According to the law of compound interest, long-term gain is what you want. Your brain overvalues short-term happiness and tries to avoid short-term pain. Caffeine is another thing that trades long-term consequences for short-term benefits. Essentially, you must, through your life, replace bad habits you unconsciously acquire with good habits, committing to become a happier person.

13. On Happiness

Confucius said that a person has two lives, and the second life begins when you realize that life is only one. So, when and how does your second life begin? (Confucius said: I never said that.) I read a quote by Blaise Pascal. It roughly means: “All of humanity’s unhappiness is because they cannot sit quietly in their rooms.” If you sit for 30 minutes and feel happy, you are successful. This is a very high state, but few people achieve it. The core skill you must learn is to be content with circumstances and go with the flow in most situations. You can get almost anything you want from life, as long as it is what you want the most. The first rule of handling conflict is: don’t be with people who frequently cause conflict. I am not interested in things that are not sustainable or difficult to sustain, including relationships full of problems.

14. The Top Priority of Life

The top priority of my life, above my happiness, above my family, above my work, is my own health. First is my physical health. Second is my mental health. Third is my spiritual health. After that, is my family’s health. After that, is my family’s happiness. After that, I can do anything else in the world that I need to do. Basically, whenever you recommend a good habit to someone, they will find an excuse for themselves, and the most common excuse is usually, “I don’t have time.” When you hear this, you know they are saying, “This is not a high-priority matter.” If something is your top priority, you will do it. That is how life works. If you have 10 to 15 vague and non-urgent matters, you will ultimately not do any of them. What I do is decide that the top priority in my life, above my happiness, above my family, above my work, is my health. My physical health has become my top priority, so I can never say I don’t have time. In the morning, I exercise, no matter how long it takes, I insist on exercising. If I haven’t finished exercising, I won’t start the day’s work. I don’t care if the world is collapsing and melting; it can wait another 30 minutes until I finish exercising. Just like other things in life, if you are willing to make short-term sacrifices, you will have long-term benefits. “Easy choice, difficult life. Difficult choice, easy life.”

15. Don’t Fight Your Own Thoughts

Don’t take yourself too seriously. You are just a monkey with a plan. Don’t make any decisions, don’t make any judgments; just accept everything. If I walk and do this for ten to fifteen minutes, I enter a very calm, grateful state. Non-judgmental consciousness is very useful to me. Another method I learned is to sit there, close my eyes, for at least an hour every day. You surrender to whatever happens—without effort. You don’t strive to do certain things, nor do you strive to oppose certain things. If thoughts flow through your mind, you flow with those thoughts. “If a thought comes, a thought comes. I don’t fight it. I don’t embrace it. I don’t think about it. I don’t reject it. I just sit there with my eyes closed for an hour, doing nothing.” This is a state of happiness, bliss, and tranquility. Once you have it, you don’t want to give it up. If you can gain an hour of happy freedom time just by sitting with your eyes closed every morning, that is priceless. It will change your life. All you have to do is sit there and do nothing. Just sit down. Close your eyes and say: “I just want to rest for an hour. This is an hour away from life, an hour where I do nothing.”

16. Let Consciousness and Mind Coexist Harmoniously

Buddhists talk about consciousness and the self; they truly view your brain as a multi-layered mechanism: a core-level operating system is running, and then there are some applications running on top of it. I am returning to the operating system of my consciousness layer, which is always calm, always peaceful, usually happy and satisfied. I try to maintain this state instead of activating the “monkey mind” (referring to the mind below consciousness). The monkey mind is always worried, afraid, and anxious; it has incredible power, but I try not to activate it until I need it. If I run it non-stop for 24 hours, I will waste energy, and the monkey mind will become me; I am more important than my monkey mind. The mind itself is a muscle—it can be trained and regulated, but it has been haphazardly trained by society into a form that we cannot control. If you examine your mind with consciousness and intention, I think you can extract your own thoughts, emotions, ideas, and reactions, and then you can start reprogramming. You can rewrite this program according to your will.

17. How to Define Wisdom?

A person understands the long-term consequences of what they do.

item.title: What are the important concepts in modern economics?
item.description:
Modern economics covers many important concepts and theories. Here are some of the main concepts:

Supply and Demand Theory: Supply and Demand Theory is one of the most fundamental concepts in economics, describing the relationship between supply and demand in the market for goods and services. It involves the formation and regulation mechanism of prices.

Marginal Analysis: Marginal Analysis emphasizes the importance of considering marginal changes in decision-making. Marginal cost, marginal utility, marginal productivity, etc., are core concepts of marginal analysis.
item.content:encoded:
Modern economics covers many important concepts and theories. Here are some of the main concepts:

Supply and Demand Theory: Supply and Demand Theory is one of the most fundamental concepts in economics, describing the relationship between supply and demand in the market for goods and services. It involves the formation and regulation mechanism of prices.

Marginal Analysis: Marginal Analysis emphasizes the importance of considering marginal changes in decision-making. Marginal cost, marginal utility, marginal productivity, etc., are core concepts of marginal analysis.

Opportunity Cost: Opportunity cost refers to the highest value of the alternative or opportunity that is given up when a certain action is chosen. It emphasizes the impact of considering opportunity cost on economic behavior.

Utility Theory: Utility Theory focuses on individual preferences and utility. It studies how individuals maximize utility when faced with choices, involving concepts such as diminishing marginal utility and utility functions.

Production Function: The production function describes the relationship between inputs and outputs, i.e., how input factors are converted into output. The production function is an important tool for studying production efficiency and output growth.

Cost Theory: Cost Theory studies the cost structure and decision-making process in a firm’s production. It includes concepts such as fixed costs, variable costs, marginal costs, etc., which are highly significant for a firm’s operational decisions.

Market Structure: Market structure studies the number, size, and interaction methods of different market participants. Common market structures include monopoly, oligopoly, competitive markets, etc.

Information Economics: Information Economics studies the transmission and utilization of information in the economy. It considers the impact of information incompleteness and asymmetry on market efficiency and resource allocation.

Externality: Externality refers to the non-market impact generated by the actions of an economic agent on others or society. Externality can be positive (positive externality) or negative (negative externality).

Public Goods: Public goods are items that cannot be excluded from individual use, and one person’s use does not affect others. Public goods usually require government intervention for provision and maintenance.
